clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old previously healthy Gilaks male presented to Rasoul Akram Hospital with acute fever (38°C) and chills. Initial vital signs showed tachycardia (HR 100), tachypnea (RR 22), and hypotension (BP 100/60). Laboratory workup revealed marked systemic inflammation with ESR 107 mm/hour (normal <15), WBC 11.1 × 10³ (normal 4–10.1), elevated cardiac markers (LDH 789 U/L, CK-MB 30 IU/L), mild anemia (Hb 10 g/dL), hyponatremia (Na 133), and hypocalcemia (Ca 7.9). Blood culture on admission was negative. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin and meropenem) were initiated by infectious disease consultation. Transoesophageal echocardiography on hospital day 5 revealed the complete pathological picture: a large semi-mobile vegetation (1.1 cm) on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp, very severe aortic regurgitation, aneurysmal aortic root (annulus 3.1 cm, sinus of Valsalva 4.2 cm), dilated ascending aorta (proximal 6.8 cm, distal 3.9 cm), and a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating 1.3 cm after the aortic valve with thickened, infected-appearing characteristics. Additional findings included reduced ejection fraction (40–45%), severe left ventricular enlargement (136 cm/m²), and mild pericardial effusion (5 mm). This constellation of findings—infective endocarditis with aortic root involvement, aneurysm, and dissection—necessitated emergent cardiac surgery. On hospital day 8, the patient underwent Bentall procedure with replacement of the aortic valve, ascending aorta, and aortic root with a mechanical composite graft (Carbomedics, size 27). Postoperatively, the patient was admitted to the cardiac ICU on warfarin and subsequently transferred to the infectious ward where antibiotic therapy was continued with ciprofloxacin, ampicillin/sulbactam, and vancomycin. At discharge around hospital day 30, laboratory values showed improvement with normalized WBC (4000 × 10³), elevated platelets (327,000 × 10³), therapeutic INR (2.6), normalized sodium (145 mEq/L), normal creatinine (0.8 mg/dL), and hemoglobin of 9.10 g/dL.
